text: /// A registry plugin's name matches exactly: `use = ["gateless_plugin"]`
/// neither wakes the dormant `gateless-plugin` nor is taken for a crate, and
/// `disable = ["gateless_plugin"]` does not block it. `auto-enable` is consent
/// for dependencies, so it wakes no registry plugin whatever the spelling.
An `[plugins] auto-enable` entry MUST NOT enable anything other than a plugin embedded in a workspace dependency.
Symposium MUST NOT activate a registry plugin that no dependency gates unless an applicable `[plugins] use` entry names it.

Symposium MUST skip, without failing, a `[plugins] use` entry that no package manager resolves.
Symposium MUST activate a dormant registry plugin while an applicable `[plugins] use` entry names it.
`cargo agents use <name>` MUST fail without changing the config when `[plugins] disable` names the package.

functions.rationale: With dormant registry plugin `gateless-plugin`: (1) `auto-enable = [gateless-plugin]` plus `use = [gateless_plugin]` leave it asleep after sync: auto-enable does not wake registry plugins (consent.auto_enable_dependencies_only), the folded use spelling does not name it (consent.registry_name_exact), so it stays dormant (consent.dormant_inactive), and the sync succeeds although `gateless_plugin` resolves to no package (consent.unresolved_use_skipped); (2) with `disable = [gateless_plugin]`, `use gateless-plugin` wakes it (consent.use_wakes_dormant; the folded disable spelling does not match: consent.registry_name_exact); (3) with the exact `disable = [gateless-plugin]`, `use gateless-plugin` fails mentioning `[plugins] disable` and the plugin stays asleep (enablement.use_disabled_rejected). Map correction: the function map listed enablement.use_unknown_rejected, but no unknown-name error is asserted here; the error asserted is the disable refusal. Citations cover every assertion. **Refuted on review:** enablement.use_syncs is applicable but not cited. Step 2 asserts `woken()` right after `use gateless-plugin` with no sync in between, so the skill is installed only because `use` syncs. Step 3's final `assert!(!woken())` holds only because the preceding `use --remove gateless-plugin` synced and reaped the skill step 2 installed; the refused `use` never syncs, and `disable` does not block registry plugins, so use_disabled_rejected alone does not explain it (the plugin was awake, not "still asleep").
